newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CROWN FIXED AT 19.400/MARK, 33.058/DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CROWN FIXED AT 19.400/MARK, 33.058/DOLLAR.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) fixed the crown at 19.400 to the mark and 33.058 to the dollar on Wednesday after fixing it at 19.500 to the mark and 30.475 to the dollar on Tuesday.
The central bank abolished a mark/dollar basket the crown was pegged to on Tuesday and said its fixing would follow the market and was only a reference point for the wider public.

The CNB let the crown fluctuatate freely under the new "controlled floating" policy, saying it would follow only the German mark as a reference point for the crown, but did not announce any details on how.
The crown has fallen sharply from the level of around 18.10 to the mark at the time of the central bank announcement on Monday evening.
Until the announcement the crown was allowed to fluctuate within a plus/minus seven percent range around the midpoint of the basket.
The central bank's steps followed a sell-off of the crown by foreign speculators and later domestic companies and the wider public.
The CNB said it was still prepared to defend the crown if necessary, adding it expected the crown to stabilise at between 17.00 and 19.50 to the mark in several months.
